text:
tanya: Heads-up: spotted weird behavior in sample-app when JSON_MODE=true + auth retry. Tool response ends up as a quoted string after the refresh and jsonschema.validate blows up. quick repro below.

`tanya: ```js
// sample-app snippet
await client.callTool({
  name: 'fetch_order',
  jsonMode: true,
  input: { order_id: 'ORD-11' },
  retry: { handleAuth: true }
});
```

vik: Which SDK? versions?

tanya: js-sdk v0.15.0-alpha, sample-app main. The logs show the tool body coming back as `"{\"status\":\"ok\",\"total\":42}"` right after a 401->refresh->retry.

aj: That looks like a double-serialize when the retry replays the response body. We had a similar fix in the py sdk where normalize_tool_output would unquote one layer.

maria: Parity concern: the ruby client treats any string-looking-json as JSON and parses it; js currently treats it as plain string. We should pick one invariant. Document it either way.

ci-bot: ci: sample-app integration tests failed (build 6789) — https://ci.internal/redwood/6789

vik: Short-term mitigation idea: in the retry middleware, if content-type indicates json OR jsonMode flag is set, run a safe unwrap: if value starts and ends with a quote and inner parses as JSON -> unquote once. Add a feature flag to toggle.

aj: Agreed on unwrap heuristic but add guard for legitimate strings: only unwrap if schema expects object/array (we can consult the provided schema). That keeps behavior deterministic.

tanya: Action items: @aj open a patch to js-sdk retry middleware + helper with tests, @maria add an e2e in sample-app/examples/json-mode-retry to exercise 401->refresh->retry, @vik coordinate a brief doc note about JSON_MODE pitfalls in onboarding guide.

maria: I'll add the test and link to an issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-app/issues/21

aj: PR incoming: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/pull/1102 (includes unit tests for unwrap and a changelog).

tanya: Nice. Once PR is green, let's run the sandbox smoke suite and then ship patch to the bootcamp branch. This bit of onboarding friction keeps tripping new users. :fistbump:
